page: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadsv7 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It includes 2835 GB of local NVMe storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included, and there are no onboard GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the E48ads_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance and gzip compression speeds, placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance, PassMark CPU scores, and database operations are strong, ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show strong write performance for large blocks and read performance for small cached blocks, though read-only bandwidth for large uncached blocks drops to average. Large-model LLM inference speeds also fall into the average tier, indicating a potential bottleneck for massive parameter models.

Given its high memory density and local storage capacity, the E48ads_v7 offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads without requiring expensive GPU resources. It is highly suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data compression tasks, and medium-scale language model inference.
